verdict.reasoning: Patient reports left-sided hearing difficulty and left facial numbness for about three weeks: "problems with my hearing... my face has been feeling a bit numb"; "Just one side, just on my left side"; "it's been a few weeks now. Um, been about three weeks or something."

Patient describes intermittent tinnitus with dizziness: "I think, occasionally noticed a, ringing in my ear" and later "like I said, like the ringing um, occasionally and, when I get that I can sometimes feel a bit dizzy."

Patient states the numbness is usually present and present now: "it kind of, kind of, there quite often, so, all the time. So yeah, right now it feels very, doesn't feel like when I touch this side of my face."

Patient denies these symptoms: limb weakness/numbness ("No, no, no, no, nothing like that."), difficulty swallowing ("No."), speech difficulties ("No, no."), vision changes ("No, that's all good."), ear discharge ("No, nothing, nothing coming out."), ear pain ("Uh, no, don't think so."), and fever ("No, nothing like that.").

Patient history: "been told I have polyps in my nose in the past" and "they said, ages ago, I had something called, can't quite remember but, labyrinthitis, something like that, but again, nothing, nothing ongoing."

Patient uses an intranasal spray PRN and does not recall its name: "I only take the, spray for my nose when I need it" and "Do you remember the name of the spray, at all?" / "Unfortunately I don't, sorry."
Patient reports using Rennies as needed: "take a Rennie's if I need to" and later "sometimes take like Rennies, but I just get that from the chemist."
Allergy documented: "Do you have any , any allergies to any medication?" / "Uh, no just Latex."
Family history: "My brother had, Neurofibromatosis, I think it is."
Occupation and impact: "Yeah, so I'm a, I'm a jockey" and "because of all the kind of, these symptoms I've been getting... I've just had to do far less training."
Living situation and pets: though there is a minor transcript glitch, the net content is that she lives with a partner and has no pets: "Um, I, uh, live with my partner." and "No, no pets."

Summary matches transcript: left hearing loss and left facial numbness ~3 weeks (as in cc-001); intermittent tinnitus and dizziness ("ringing... occasionally" and "sometimes feel a bit dizzy"), and absence of fever or other focal deficits (multiple denials). Doctor suggests Bell’s palsy and in-person exam: "what you're describing might be something called Bell's Palsy" and plans neuro exam and ear exam.

Same-day face-to-face exam planned including neuro and ear exam: "I would like you to be assessed in a clinic today"; "I would like a GP to assess you... we can do a... neurological examination" and "Have a look, have a look inside the ear, see if there's any... to see within the ear." Cranial nerves are part of neuro exam and are reasonably implied.

Admin and booking process: "I'm gonna send a message to our admin team, I'll ask them, to book you in for a face-to-face appointment in one of our clinics"; "within Central London"; "I'll leave that number in your notes. And you can ring them after five minutes, and then they'll slot you in to a place that's convenient for you."

Reassurance and emphasis on attending: "this doesn't seem to be you know, anything um, that you're gonna die from"; "that's not usually a life-threatening problem"; "preliminarily I can, I can reassure you" and "please make sure the appointment gets done today."
